reason: The text clearly demonstrates that non-leaders possess and exercise agency. The servant (נַעַר) accompanying Saul actively participates in decision-making—he suggests consulting the seer (9:6), volunteers his own money as payment (9:8), and influences Saul's course of action. Similarly, the young women at the well (נְעָר֔וֹת) exercise agency by providing crucial information and directions (9:11-13). Even before Saul is anointed king, he demonstrates agency in proposing the plan to visit Samuel (9:6-7). Multiple non-leader characters make meaningful choices and decisions that directly shape the narrative. Only a leader (Samuel) and God possess ultimate authority, but agency is clearly distributed among various characters regardless of their hierarchical position.
